incident_a_pool_exhaustion.root_cause: Connection pool exhaustion in payment-gateway-adapter caused by deployment v2.4.1 (which reduced the connection pool size from 50 to 10), leading to ConnectionPoolTimeoutException and intermittent 504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT charge failures under normal traffic.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Multiple ConnectionPoolTimeoutException errors in payment-gateway-adapter following deployment: '2026-09-02 14:47:12 ERROR payment-gateway-adapter  ConnectionPoolTimeoutException: no available connection after 5000ms' and resulting GATEWAY_TIMEOUT in payment-service.
v2.4.1 (2026-09-02 14:30) on payment-gateway-adapter: Reduced connection pool size from 50 to 10 (memory optimization for the upcoming cost-reduction initiative)

KI-101: A ConnectionPoolTimeoutException in payment-gateway-adapter logs is a known signature of an undersized connection pool relative to current traffic; cross-reference against deployment history for any recent pool size change — Recurred more than once - see previous incidents; both prior occurrences traced back to a pool size reduction

INC-2031 (2026-03-14): Intermittent payment failures due to connection pool size set too low for peak traffic during deploy configuration change. Resolved by reverting pool size to 50 (MTTR: 22 minutes).

RB-014 (Payment Gateway Timeout Spike): Symptoms match ConnectionPoolTimeoutException; Remediation: revert pool size to prior baseline (50 connections) and redeploy payment-gateway-adapter. Typical MTTR: 20 minutes.
payment-gateway-adapter owns a bounded connection pool to the external Payment Provider's API; synchronous dependency for payment-service.

incident_a_pool_exhaustion.remediation: Revert the connection pool size configuration in payment-gateway-adapter from 10 back to the historical baseline of 50 connections (or scale up to match peak load) and redeploy payment-gateway-adapter.

incident_b_ambiguous_delay.root_cause: Suspected message queue processing backlog or third-party email provider delivery latency affecting notification-service; root cause is unconfirmed due to lack of per-stage instrumentation, absence of error logs, zero correlated deployments, and no matching known issues or prior incidents.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-15 11:10:02 WARN notification-service Queue depth elevated: 340 messages (with observed 40-75 minute lag between Email queued and Email sent, but no error logs or failed deliveries).
No deployment touched notification-service in the month before this incident (2026-08-15); no correlated deployment found.
No previous incident in historical record involves notification-service email delivery latency; first recorded report of this symptom.
RB-002 (Elevated Notification Queue Depth): Note indicates runbook is incomplete pending better instrumentation; consumer/downstream bottleneck is unverified.
notification-service consumes internal message queue; consumer pool size and third-party email provider latency are uninstrumented with per-stage timing.

incident_b_ambiguous_delay.remediation: Verify consumer worker count and downstream third-party email provider latency; scale notification-service consumers if worker pool starvation is confirmed, and add per-stage latency metrics and monitoring to notification-service.
